caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 440 of 2000
lawyer:
MI Faruqui with SM Munir, Md Ruhul Quddus, Advocates ----- For the Appellants 
Abdul Quayum. Deputy Attorney-General ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Khandkar Abul Hussain -----Appellant
Vs.
Government of the peoples Republic of Bangladesh and others -----Opposite parties
full_judgment:
Md Awlad Ali J: This Appeal by the plaintiff arises out of Judgment and decree dated 29-9-99 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 20/95 by which the plaint of the suit was rejected. 

 ii) 	To pass a money decree amounts to Taka 3,67,00,000.00 as detailed in the schedule below with 15% interest per annum in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants as damages and compensation for the torts they committed jointly and severally. 

 4. The plaintiff has further averred that the Bureau of Anti-Corruption filed on FIR being Ramna PS Case No. 90 dated January, 21, 1991 and under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and sections 5(II) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the Government Officers including the plaintiff for causing financial loss of Taka 32,42,50,200 to the Government of Bangladesh. The plaintiff claims that he was falsely implicated in the said criminal case by the Government defendant to cause severe damage to the reputation of the plaintiff and the members of his family. The defendant Government officials highlighted and projected the false allegation of corruption which was also circulated by the local and foreign media. The false case against the plaintiff was widely published in Bangladesh through different electronic and press media in the form of "Government Handcut" most illegally with malafide motive to lower him down in the cadre of service to obstruct the promotion. On the basis of Government statement a news was published on 23rd January, 1991 in Thailand's widely circulated and well respected English daily newspaper "The Bangkok Post" under the caption Bangladesh charges ex-Minister, three officials with corruption which has specifically mentioned the name and designation and place of posting of the plaintiff. Thus the plaintiff along with his family members were illegally maligned and socially humiliated both at home and at Bangkok where the plaintiff and his wife were enjoying diplomatic status by the defendants concerned who acted malafide and are responsible for damaging reputation of the plaintiff. It is further alleged that the second Government handout dated July, 1st, 1991 relating to the case published in the newspaper and broadcast in Radio and Television dropped the name of the plaintiff but delibecately did not clarify about the non-involvement and innocence of the plaintiff in the case. On the contrary on 15th July, 1991 while the plaintiff was in Bangkok another news item was widely published in Bangladesh under the caption ''Corruption charge against 132 accomplices of Ershad", The list of alleged corrupt officers was published in that news item including the name of the plaintiff as well. Consequent upon such publicity of false allegations the plaintiff was first debarred from appearing at the test for promotion as Joint Secretary along within the Officers of his batch of 1964 in October/November, 1991. By widely published anti-corruption case in which the plaintiff was falsely implicated and unjustly down-graded his ACR and oral test marks just to find an excuse to deprive his of his due promotion. For this unfounded anti-corruption case the principal defendant were responsible for damages caused to the plaintiff. On the above allegation the plaintiff sought for a decree for money amounting to Taka 3,67,000.00 with 15% interest as damages and compensation for the torts the defendants had committed jointly and severally. 

 10. In this view the Judgment and decrees passed by the learned Subordinate Judge rejecting the plaint as a while is not justified and cannot be sustained in law. Accordingly, the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is set aside. When two distinct causes founded on distinct and separate allegations are brought before the court and if one cause is clearly barred under any provision of law the Court is authorised under the law and can legitimately try other cause for granting relief which is not related to the barring provision. The case is accordingly remanded back to the learned Subordinate Judge for spliting up the suit and try the cause which is relating to the claim for damages for defamation and for tortous liability of the defendants. The plaintiff will also be at liberty to amend the plaint for seeking proper relief which the Civil Court can competently grant.
